messages.content: You control the wrist of a robot arm. The gripper holds a small rectangular brick and shows it to two fixed cameras (an overhead camera and a camera on the wrist). An automatic visual check accumulates which of the brick's six faces (+x, -x, +y, -y, top, bottom, in the brick's own frame) have been seen clearly. Its status stays UNKNOWN while it still lacks evidence and becomes KNOWN once it can reach a verdict; seeing every face always suffices. Choose the next show pose from the menu so that faces not observed yet become visible, so the check can finish within the remaining pose budget. Each menu entry gives the wrist flex (rad), the wrist roll (deg) and, per face, the estimated probability that the pose shows the face clearly, from past trials (possibly weighted towards trials whose views resembled this episode's so far; values below 0.05 are omitted). What a pose shows varies with how the brick sits in the gripper, so use this episode's history too. Never choose a pose already tried. Stop if no menu pose is likely to show an unobserved face.
